newsitem.title: UK: Copper ends LME stable, contango narrows.
newsitem.headline: Copper ends LME stable, contango narrows.

text.p: Forward copper prices backtracked in Wednesday afternoon LME trading to end little changed as the market again failed to challenge $1,950 overhead.
But the main feature was a narrowing in the newly-established contango, traders said.

Profit-taking and expectations of bank and US broker selling prevented the market pushing higher in the afternoon, but cash metal buying and borrowing interst reduced the cash/threes contango to $3/5 from Tuesday's $9.

Some traders said that recent warrant business and physical offtake suggests that the contango could revert to a backwardation again, as stocks are likely to register another significant decline on Friday.
Whether this helps the forward market break higher is open to question, however, as the $1,950 level may be defended until after next week's October declarations, others said.
Final kerb business was at $1,922 a tonne, down from a $1,944 peak, and just $2 up from Tuesday's kerb.
The action in the rest of the metal complex was low-key as most markets are uncertain in the short-term, traders said.
Aluminium was hesitant throughout, as prices have been unable to make any real headway back above $1,400. This suggests that another test of the downside is likely, traders said.
Final kerb trade today was at $1,400 a tonne, with business conducted in a tight $1,397/1,403 band throughout the session.
Nickel prices settled back from midsession highs, although the market remained broadly stable throughout the afternoon session. Last trade was at $7,260, up $45 from Tuesday.
After the market closed news emerged that talks are to resume at Inco's Manitoba, where a lock-out currently prevails.
Lead prices drifted back from morning highs of $784 in sluggish trading, against a background of slow European physical offtake. Three months concluded the kerb at $779, against a previous $780.

The zinc market has been content to fluctuate either side of $1,020 recently, and Wednesday was no exception with prices trending slightly lower during the latter part of the session. The market ended at an unchanged $1,018.
Tin business was more encouraging, with prices moving up and away from the $6,000 level, albeit in slow conditions. Last business was at $6,085, up $35 a tonne.
The alloy market hardly traded, and closed at $1,225/30, against Tuesday's $1,235 a tonne. -- Martin Hayes, London newsroom 44 171 542 8080
